Move the light

The blacklight case

Some of it glows.

Uranium glass — "vaseline glass" — was made with a pinch of the real thing from the 1880s to the 1940s, and it lights up green under blacklight. CC's keeps a case of it lit. Run your light over the shelves.

CC

What's inside

What are you hunting for?

Thirty-some dealers, each booth its own little shop. Tap a category and we'll tell you what's here and which floor to head for.

The glass is the reason people drive out.

Cases of uranium glass lit so it glows, cobalt and cranberry Depression glass by the shelf, cut crystal, fine china and the odd teapot you didn't know you needed. Regulars say it's the most organized glass they've seen in an antique store — nothing's buried.

  • Uranium / vaseline glass
  • Cobalt & cranberry
  • Depression glass
  • Fine china
  • Cut crystal
Main floor · the lit cases

Real wood. Real weight.

Dining tables, sideboards, desks and the kind of chairs nobody makes anymore — set out on rugs so you can see them as rooms, not a warehouse. If it's big, the staff will help you get it to the car.

  • Dining & occasional tables
  • Desks & sideboards
  • Chairs & rockers
  • Rugs

Toys you grew up with, and a NASCAR corner.

"Brings back memories" is the most common thing people say here — tin toys, kitchen gadgets, records, paper. And there's a dedicated NASCAR collection, which is not something you find in every small-town antique mall.

Table lamps with their original shades, mirrors, art, and home décor arranged by theme and color so you can walk a wall and find your palette. Bring a photo of your room.

The story

A department store, re-stocked.

The building at 1501 Cole went up in 1925 as Enumclaw's J.C. Penney. A century later it's still a place you come to browse two floors under one roof — except now every corner belongs to a different dealer, and every dealer has a thing they're nuts about.

That's what makes CC's different from a shop with one owner's taste: 30-plus little shops inside one, curated, tagged and arranged by color and theme, with a front counter that's seen it all (and keeps a basket of little rubber animals for the kids).

The Courier-Herald readers voted it Best Antiques & Collectibles on the Plateau. Owner [PLACEHOLDER — owner name] has kept the doors open since [PLACEHOLDER — year opened].
